explanation:
[EFFECT] Month has a non-monotonic effect. Winter months are negative drivers: January (~–0.25) and February (~–0.20) most strongly suppress demand. Contributions rise through spring, are near zero in summer (July–August), and peak in autumn — especially October (~+0.35 to +0.37) — before easing in November and December.
[IMPORTANCE] Fourth in importance (0.086); a moderate influence, spanning roughly 0.6 log units.
[RECOMMENDATION] Hour of day and temperature are by far the two strongest drivers of predicted demand, so operational planning — such as bike redistribution and staffing — should be tightly organised around the two daily rush-hour peaks (around 8 a.m. and 5–6 p.m.) and scaled up noticeably in mild to warm weather while scaling back during cold spells or the early hours of the morning.
